title: An overview of Webdriver.io, Nightwatch, Puppeteer, Jasmine, Jest, Robot and QA Wolf

videos.script: Lesson eight was Selenium, lesson nine Cypress, lesson ten Playwright. This lesson names seven more tools. It is a map, not seven tutorials. {{layers}} Every browser test is built in layers. A runner finds the tests and reports on them. A library turns your code into commands. A protocol carries those commands. And a browser obeys them. {{protocols}} Three protocols matter. WebDriver is the W3C standard that Selenium speaks. WebDriver BiDi is its newer, two-way version. And the Chrome DevTools Protocol is spoken only by Chromium browsers. {{puppeteer}} You run one tool for real. Puppeteer opens the shop, adds a banana and reads the basket, in a dozen lines. Then you take out one wait, and watch it give two different answers. {{compare}} Next you set it beside Playwright, line by line. Playwright's first authors came from Puppeteer, and the differences show what they learned. {{others}} WebdriverIO and Nightwatch are WebDriver tools with runners of their own. Jest and Jasmine are runners that drive no browser at all. Robot Framework writes tests as keywords. And QA Wolf is a company that writes and runs your tests for you. {{choice}} By the end, you can place each one on the map. And you will see why most teams pick the tool that fits what they already use.
